newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr closes weaker after bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr closes weaker after bank intervention.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed at C$1.3994 (US$0.7145) in moderate trading on Monday after the Bank of Canada intervened to support the currency at the C$1.3995 (US$0.7145) level, traders said.
* They said the currency weakened in a late afternoon attempt by offshore sellers to push the unit to C$1.4000 (US$0.7142).
Analysts said the markets would now focus on key U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data due to be released on Tuesday.
A Reuters poll predicted that U.S CPI would rise by 0.2 percent in March and CPI excluding food and energy would increase 0.3 percent for the same month.
Signs of U.S. inflationary pressures could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates as it did on March 25.

"Core CPI is the critical number here," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist for Lehman Brothers. "People are really worried, and the Canadian dollar could once again feel the heat of that."

A 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed on March 25 widened the spread between U.S. and Canadian short-term rates to more than 200 points, pressuring the Canadian dollar and renewing calls for the Bank of Canada to follow suit.
The Canada dollar would be pressured as long as the interest rate speculation haunted the market, Gregory said.

The release of Canada's federal budget deficit figures on Monday, which showed a drop of C$485 million to C$2.31 billion in February, also failed to shield the Canada dollar against the weak tide, traders said.
"The deficit numbers are priced in," one trader said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2362 marks from Friday's close of 1.2309 marks and jumped to 90.38 yen from Friday's 90.20 yen.
